audit.whatIsWrong: The entry claims five separate times that K'Sante's passive deals percent-max-HP damage ('percent-max-HP damage on every empowered auto', 'percent-max-HP shred', 'percent-HP autos', 'his percent-HP scaling'). Dauntless Instinct reads: 'K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack.' There is no percent-health component anywhere in his kit — the kit file carries no percentHealth flag on any K'Sante ability.
audit.why: This is the load-bearing premise of the whole early game section, and it is invented. It also produces the wrong conclusion: a Teemo told his HP bar is unsafe regardless will play the lane far too passively for a matchup he wins 55%.
audit.corrected: Dauntless Instinct is an ability-then-auto pattern: he lands a spell to mark you, then his next attack hits harder. Blinding Dart eats exactly that attack.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (P Dauntless Instinct; no percentHealth flag on any ability)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly calls Path Maker (W) a shield that 'absorbs your Q dart' / 'absorbs your Q blind'. W is a charge-up that takes reduced damage and then dashes with a knockback and stun. The shield in K'Sante's kit is Footwork (E).
audit.why: Two errors compound: the ability is misidentified, and damage reduction cannot absorb a blind at all — blind is a debuff application, not damage. A Teemo who holds Q 'until after the W block' is holding it for a block that does not exist.
audit.corrected: W is a damage-reduction charge into a dash, knockback and stun. E Footwork (10/9.5/9/8.5/8) is the shield. Blind applies through both.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (W Path Maker; E Footwork 'dashes and gains a shield')

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that All Out's opening knockback launches you through any wall in its path, and that once All Out is active Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns.
audit.why: Teemo has no dash. Being launched through terrain into K'Sante's jungle is the single way this matchup ends badly, and it is entirely positional — you avoid it by not laning with your back to a wall. The second half is the good news nobody tells you: after he ults, his W stops CCing.
audit.corrected: Never stand with a wall behind you when All Out is up. Once he is All Out, Path Maker is damage only — no knockback, no stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R: 'launching them through any wall in their path'; W: 'When All Out ... no longer knocks back or stuns')

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out's self-cost is mentioned as a threat ('All Out strips his own resistances and he becomes a fighter who can actually kill you') but never as an opportunity.
audit.why: The kit is explicit that All Out grants its damage and healing 'at the cost of reduced defenses'. For a champion whose entire damage profile is a magic-damage DoT, the moment his resistances drop is the moment his poison clock speeds up. Framing it purely as a threat inverts the actual play.
audit.corrected: All Out cuts his own defenses. That is when Toxic Shot and Liandry's burn fastest — the answer is anti-heal plus distance, not disengage on reflex.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R: 'at the cost of reduced defenses')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, even though All Out grants healing and the flagged missing interaction for this matchup is needs-antiheal.
audit.why: Teemo's damage is a damage-over-time trickle, which is the profile healing counters hardest. Anti-heal timing decides every extended trade after 6.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal before the second full item, not after.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'mid' says 'your Q max rank means every blinded window is eight full seconds where his percent-HP autos deal zero damage', describing levels 4-5.
audit.why: Three errors stacked: Q rank 5 needs level 9; Teemo's Q cooldown is a flat 7 at every rank, not 8; and the sentence uses the cooldown number as if it were the blind duration.
audit.corrected: Q is rank 3 at best at level 5, on a flat 7s cooldown at every rank. The blind lasts a fraction of that.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q cooldown '7' — single value, all ranks)

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0] is titled 'Get walled by his Q'. Ntofo Strikes does not create or launch through walls; All Out does. The descriptions under dontsFull[0], dontsFull[1] and dosFull[2] are all template text belonging to other slots.
audit.why: A player scanning the Don'ts list learns to fear the wrong ability and gets no explanation of the one that actually kills them.
audit.corrected: The wall interaction is R. Point each description at its own heading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The layers disagree on the level chart at five of seven stages. content win = [K'Sante, K'Sante, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Skill, K'Sante]; full phases sides = [Skill, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Teemo]. The full layer also labels the matchup 'EVEN' at 6/10 while the packet shows 55% over 500 games.
audit.why: The same page renders both. A reader sees Level 6 as Teemo in one chart and Skill in the other, and the two-item stage as K'Sante in one and Teemo in the other.
audit.corrected: I am NOT proposing side flips here — the content layer's own whys genuinely argue for 'Skill' at levels 3, 4-5 and first item, so the disagreement is real and needs a human call rather than an auto-align. Reporting it instead.

edits.before: K'Sante's passive deals percent-max-HP damage on every empowered auto, so he wins pure auto trades before your Q blind is available for every exchange.
edits.after: Dauntless Instinct marks you with an ability, then his NEXT attack hits harder — it is not percent-HP shred. Blind that one attack and the whole pattern collapses.

edits.before: Liandry's Angueur makes your E poison eat through his tank HP on a timer — he cannot stand still to block-absorb poke and his W shield has a long cooldown.
edits.after: Liandry's makes your E poison eat his HP on a timer, and his real shield is Footwork (E) at 10-8s, not Path Maker — W is a damage-reduction charge, not a block.

edits.before: Blind his empowered-auto windows with Q to negate passive percent-HP procs and deny his W-shield trades
edits.after: Blind the attack that follows each of his abilities — Dauntless Instinct loads damage into that one auto

edits.before: Use W to dash through a mushroom or absorb your Q dart, then close with Q3 knockup for a full all-in window
edits.after: Charge Path Maker (W) through your poke for the knockback and stun, then Q into the shockwave pull for a full all-in

edits.before: K'Sante's passive percent-HP autos make Level 1 auto trades pure losses for you — last-hit at E poison range and never walk into auto-swap distance before his W is visibly on cooldown.
edits.after: K'Sante loads damage into the attack after each ability, so level 1 auto trades go to him — last-hit at poison range and step out of attack range the instant a spell lands on you.

edits.before: His W shield absorbs your Q blind at Level 2 and he immediately dashes in for a free trade — hold Q until after his W animation so your blind actually lands on empowered autos.
edits.after: Path Maker takes reduced damage while charging, so poke into the charge is wasted — but blind still applies through it, and the stun-dash it ends in is what you must be out of range of.

edits.before: Mushrooms seal both flanking bushes and the river path, so his All Out dash commits into a slow-and-reveal — his engage is now a telegraphed gap-close you can Q-blind mid-air and W away from.
edits.after: Mushrooms seal both flanking bushes and the river path, so his All Out dash commits into a slow-and-reveal — and the wall-launch on its first hit is the reason you never lane with terrain at your back.

edits.before: K'Sante's passive turns every auto he lands into percent-max-HP shred — at Level 1 you cannot win a straight auto trade before your Q is off cooldown, and he will happily stack those procs to chunk you down. At Level 2 his W shield can absorb your Q dart clean and then he dashes into you for free; respect this window by holding your blind for when his W is clearly on cooldown, not preemptively throwing it into the block. The good news is that he cannot kill you without burning All Out, which is a long-cooldown ult — farm conservatively with E poison autos, accept that the health bar favours him early, and do not let the chip lead bait you into fighting on his terms.
edits.after: K'Sante's passive loads damage into the attack that follows an ability, not into percent-max-HP shred — so at Level 1 you lose a straight auto trade, but only while he can reach you. Last-hit at range and step back the moment a spell marks you. At Level 2 his Path Maker charge takes reduced damage, which means poking into the charge is wasted; blind still applies through it, so save Q for the dash arriving rather than throwing it at the wind-up. His shield is Footwork (E), on 10-8s, and that is the cooldown worth tracking early. He cannot kill you without All Out, a 120/100/80s ultimate — farm conservatively with poison autos and let the chip lead build.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a contested control window: his W shield and Q3 pull are dangerous but telegraphed, and your Q max rank means every blinded window is eight full seconds where his percent-HP autos deal zero damage. Hold the wave on your side of the river so he must walk up to CS, then poke with E, Q when he reaches auto range, and W back before his Q3 pull lands. At Level 6 the lane shifts decisively your way — mushrooms on both tribush entrances and the dragon-side pixel brush mean his All Out dash cannot reach you without triggering a slow and reveal; any dash commit that hits shrooms gives you time to W disengage or force a blinded all-in on your terms.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are contested: Q is rank 3 at best (rank 5 needs level 9) on a flat 7s cooldown, so blind uptime is fixed and each cast has to be spent on the attack that follows one of his abilities. Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5s cooldown at 450 range and its third cast pulls you in, so hold the wave your side and stay past that line. At Level 6 the lane shifts your way — mushrooms on both tribush entrances and the dragon-side brush mean All Out cannot reach you unrevealed. Watch your back: its opening knockback launches you through any wall behind you, and Teemo has no dash to come back. Footwork (E) at 10-8s is his shield and his second dash — count it before you commit.

edits.before: Late game K'Sante reclaims the 1v1 — All Out turns him into a fighter with execute-range damage and his percent-HP scaling means your HP bar is not safe even through Liandry's stacks. Avoid ever taking a solo fight against a Iceborn-Gauntlet K'Sante without shrooms pre-placed on every exit, because the slow field removes your W kite. Your value shifts to split-push pressure in a shroom-warded side lane: he cannot safely solo-clear a lane you have fully mined, and his teamfight range is short enough that your team can fight 4v4 while he is stuck peeling through mushroom fields chasing you.
edits.after: Late game K'Sante reclaims the 1v1 — All Out gives him fighter damage and healing, so Grievous Wounds is not optional here, it is what makes your DoT count. The trade-off is his: All Out runs at reduced defenses, so a K'Sante who ults into you is the softest he ever gets against magic damage. Never duel an Iceborn-Gauntlet K'Sante without shrooms on every exit, because the slow field removes your kite. Your value is split pressure in a mined side lane he cannot safely clear. Once he is All Out, Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns, so that follow-up CC is gone.

edits.after: Shroom and poison him early — blind his post-ability auto. Anti-heal before All Out.

notes: Same champion-wide name defects apply here as on every Teemo matchup: "Blinding Shot" x271 in champ-data/content/teemo.js should be Blinding Dart, and "Liandry's Angueur" x80 is not an item name (teemo.full.js uses Liandry's Torment). Both need one global replace, not per-matchup proposals. MATCHUP-SPECIFIC WARNING: the fabricated 'percent-max-HP' claim about K'Sante appears in five separate strings in this one entry, which suggests a generator that assigned a %HP damage profile to tanks by category. Worth grepping other Teemo tank matchups (Cho'Gath, Sion, Ornn, Malphite) for the same phrase before trusting them — I found the identical pattern here with no kit basis at all. I did not propose level-chart side flips despite a five-of-seven disagreement between the layers, because the content whys genuinely argue for their side; that one needs a human call.
